use: Usually moyamoya suru: a nagging feeling you can't put your finger on.

example.romaji: nanka moyamoya suru n da yo ne.
example.ja: なんかモヤモヤするんだよね。
example.english: Something just doesn't sit right with me.

examplePolite.romaji: nan da ka moyamoya shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: なんだかモヤモヤします。
examplePolite.english: Something just doesn't sit right with me.

notes: Literally hazy or misty, like a blur in your vision.

use: Usually ukiuki suru: light, bouncy happiness before something nice, like a trip.

example.romaji: ashita ryokou da kara ukiuki shiteru.
example.ja: 明日旅行だからウキウキしてる。
example.english: I'm all excited because I'm going on a trip tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita ryokou na node ukiuki shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 明日旅行なのでウキウキしています。
examplePolite.english: I'm all excited because I'm going on a trip tomorrow.

notes: Close to wakuwaku; ukiuki is a lighter mood that shows on the outside.

use: Says something is fully ready or went exactly right.

example.romaji: junbi wa batchiri da yo.
example.ja: 準備はばっちりだよ。
example.english: Everything's all set.

examplePolite.romaji: junbi wa batchiri desu.
examplePolite.ja: 準備はばっちりです。
examplePolite.english: Everything's all set.

notes: Also before a verb: batchiri mieta (saw it clearly), batchiri neta (slept perfectly).

use: For a quick once-over (zatto miru) or a ballpark figure.

example.romaji: zatto me o tooshite oite.
example.ja: ざっと目を通しておいて。
example.english: Give it a quick look-over.

examplePolite.romaji: zatto me o tooshite oite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: ざっと目を通しておいてください。
examplePolite.english: Please give it a quick look-over.

notes: With numbers it means 'about': zatto sanjuu nin (roughly thirty people).

use: Usually X-go ga perapera (fluent in a language).

example.romaji: kanojo, eigo perapera da yo ne.
example.ja: 彼女、英語ペラペラだよね。
example.english: She speaks fluent English, doesn't she?

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo wa eigo ga perapera desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女は英語がペラペラですね。
examplePolite.english: Her English is fluent, isn't it.

notes: Also talking too much or blabbing secrets (perapera shaberu), and thin flimsy paper.

use: For patient, unglamorous effort over time, like saving or studying.

example.romaji: mainichi kotsukotsu benkyou shiteru n da.
example.ja: 毎日コツコツ勉強してるんだ。
example.english: I study a little bit every day.

examplePolite.romaji: mainichi kotsukotsu benkyou shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 毎日コツコツ勉強しています。
examplePolite.english: I study a little bit every day.

notes: Also the sound of tapping or heels on a hard floor.

use: For trains, shops or roads with hardly anyone in them.

example.romaji: kyou no densha, garagara datta ne.
example.ja: 今日の電車、ガラガラだったね。
example.english: The train was nearly empty today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou no densha wa garagara deshita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日の電車はガラガラでしたね。
examplePolite.english: The train was nearly empty today.

notes: Also a hoarse voice (koe ga garagara) and a rattling sound, like a sliding door. Opposite: gyuugyuu or konde iru.

use: For a room, hair or thoughts in a mess, or food gone soggy.

example.romaji: heya ga guchagucha da yo.
example.ja: 部屋がぐちゃぐちゃだよ。
example.english: The room's a total mess.

examplePolite.romaji: heya ga guchagucha de sumimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 部屋がぐちゃぐちゃですみません。
examplePolite.english: Sorry the room's such a mess.

notes: Feelings too: atama no naka ga guchagucha (my head's a mess). Close to mechakucha.

use: With squeezing or holding verbs: gyutto dakishimeru (hug tight), gyutto nigiru (grip tight).

example.romaji: te o gyutto nigitte kureta.
example.ja: 手をぎゅっと握ってくれた。
example.english: She squeezed my hand tight.

examplePolite.romaji: te o gyutto nigitte kuremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 手をぎゅっと握ってくれました。
examplePolite.english: She squeezed my hand tight.

notes: Gyuu alone is a hug in casual talk (gyuu shite = hug me).

use: For a train, bag or schedule crammed full.

example.romaji: asa no densha, gyuugyuu da yo.
example.ja: 朝の電車、ぎゅうぎゅうだよ。
example.english: The morning train is packed.

examplePolite.romaji: asa no densha wa gyuugyuu desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 朝の電車はぎゅうぎゅうですね。
examplePolite.english: The morning train is packed, isn't it.

notes: Gyuugyuu zume = crammed in like sardines.

use: Praise for fluffy food, hair, towels or bedding.

example.romaji: kono pankeeki, fuwafuwa da ne!
example.ja: このパンケーキ、ふわふわだね!
example.english: This pancake is so fluffy!

examplePolite.romaji: kono pankeeki, fuwafuwa desu ne!
examplePolite.ja: このパンケーキ、ふわふわですね!
examplePolite.english: This pancake is so fluffy!

notes: Also floating, or a dreamy, light-headed mood (fuwafuwa suru).

english: light and crispy; quickly and smoothly
use: For light, crisp food like tempura or cookies.

example.romaji: kono tenpura, sakusaku de oishii.
example.ja: この天ぷら、サクサクでおいしい。
example.english: This tempura is nice and crispy.

examplePolite.romaji: kono tenpura wa sakusaku de oishii desu.
examplePolite.ja: この天ぷらはサクサクでおいしいです。
examplePolite.english: This tempura is nice and crispy.

notes: Second sense: things moving fast and smoothly, like work (shigoto ga sakusaku susumu) or an app.

use: Praise for soft, bouncy food like mochi, bread or noodles.

example.romaji: kono udon, mochimochi de oishii ne.
example.ja: このうどん、もちもちでおいしいね。
example.english: These udon are nice and chewy.

examplePolite.romaji: kono udon wa mochimochi de oishii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: このうどんはもちもちでおいしいですね。
examplePolite.english: These udon are nice and chewy.

notes: Always a compliment, unlike English 'chewy'. Also soft, plump skin: mochimochi hada.

use: Usually kotteri shita: rich, oily or thick flavour, like ramen broth.

example.romaji: kyou wa kotteri shita raamen ga tabetai.
example.ja: 今日はこってりしたラーメンが食べたい。
example.english: I want some rich, heavy ramen today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa kotteri shita raamen ga tabetai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日はこってりしたラーメンが食べたいです。
examplePolite.english: I'd like some rich, heavy ramen today.

notes: The opposite is assari (light, plain). Kotteri shiborareta = got a real chewing out.

use: For thin, crackly things: seaweed, chips, fresh lettuce, crisp chicken skin.

example.romaji: nori ga paripari de oishii.
example.ja: 海苔がパリパリでおいしい。
example.english: The seaweed's nice and crisp.

examplePolite.romaji: nori ga paripari de oishii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 海苔がパリパリでおいしいです。
examplePolite.english: The seaweed's nice and crisp.

notes: Sakusaku is light and airy; paripari is thin and snappy; a hard crunch is karikari.

use: For something polished or brand new; often pikapika ni suru (make it spotless).

example.romaji: kuruma, pikapika ni shita yo.
example.ja: 車、ピカピカにしたよ。
example.english: I got the car sparkling clean.

examplePolite.romaji: kuruma o pikapika ni shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 車をピカピカにしました。
examplePolite.english: I got the car sparkling clean.

notes: Pikapika no ichinensei = a brand-new first-grader. Also lights flashing (pikapika hikaru).

use: For hair, sand or skin that's smooth and dry, not sticky.

example.romaji: kami, sarasara da ne.
example.ja: 髪、さらさらだね。
example.english: Your hair is so silky.

examplePolite.romaji: kami ga sarasara desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 髪がさらさらですね。
examplePolite.english: Your hair is so silky.

notes: Also a stream flowing, or writing without effort (sarasara kaku). Opposite of betobeto.

use: For clothes, hair or people soaked by rain or a spill.

example.romaji: ame de bishobisho ni natta.
example.ja: 雨でびしょびしょになった。
example.english: I got soaked in the rain.

examplePolite.romaji: ame de bishobisho ni narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 雨でびしょびしょになりました。
examplePolite.english: I got soaked in the rain.

notes: Bishonure means the same.

use: For slick surfaces like an icy road, and very smooth skin.

example.romaji: michi ga tsurutsuru da kara ki o tsukete.
example.ja: 道がつるつるだから気をつけて。
example.english: The road is slippery, so be careful.

examplePolite.romaji: michi ga tsurutsuru desu kara ki o tsukete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 道がつるつるですから気をつけてください。
examplePolite.english: The road is slippery, so please be careful.

notes: Also slurping noodles: soba o tsurutsuru taberu.

use: For sticky hands, sweaty skin or a greasy table.

example.romaji: te ga betobeto da, aratte kuru.
example.ja: 手がベトベトだ、洗ってくる。
example.english: My hands are sticky, I'll go wash them.

examplePolite.romaji: te ga betobeto na node, aratte kimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 手がベトベトなので、洗ってきます。
examplePolite.english: My hands are sticky, so I'll go wash them.

notes: Nebaneba is gooey and stringy, like natto; betobeto is unpleasantly sticky.
